flags.summary: The sales manager instructs the closer that no prospect may end a call undecided, and frames allowing a prospect to think it over as the rep being selfish.
evidence: I don't want to see any more calls where you let them off the hook.

you have to start showing up as a leader on these calls and get back to that point of getting people to a clear yes or no. When I listen to the next calls that you have today, it needs to be a clear yes or no.
That's where we need to be at, is don't let people hop off the call. Choose courage and fight through it.
If you let anybody hop off the call with a sleep, think about it, or anything like that, that's selfish. Yeah. It's actually selfish.
Fortunately, you can't sleep on it because it's not a mattress

flags.summary: The manager coaches the closer to assume every prospect holds credit cards and treat that as a positive signal, citing having previously helped a client obtain a 0% credit card in order to fund a $6,000 purchase.
evidence: I remember I had a lady for this mindset program... she was like, yeah, I really want to put this on a credit card. And I helped her get an Amex card that was 0%. And so she got the card, like, two days later in the mail, and she piffed. Like, 6k.

it doesn't serve you to think that people won't have these things. It actually serves you more to think that they do. Like, to just assume that everybody has credit cards and that's a normal thing is only going to serve you. It's not going to hurt you. It's a green flag, you know?
Most people just take care of it up front, put it on a credit card.
FINANCIAL PICTURE probing coached live: 'so at the end of each month, after all your bills are paid, all of that, how much is left over at the end of each month?'

flags.summary: A prospect with hip joint damage who is taking a six-month sabbatical for mental and physical health is discussed purely as a closing problem, with the manager treating the mental-health sabbatical as additional reason to sell him, and neither party raising whether loaded kettlebell training is suitable for the joint damage.
evidence: The objection was, I'm taking six months off work in a week. / To focus on what? / Mental health and physical health. / But that's more reason for him to do the program.
he's in pain and he doesn't believe he can get out of pain, because he's got hip joint damage and he's a surgeon
I listened to the tail end of it after the price drop and immediately it was very clear that this guy probably would have closed
If you would have just did an open wallet and gotten clear on his finances and then probably pitched him like a six pay.

flags.summary: The closer states he booked 15 deals in the month with only 3 paid in full, a volume and payment-mix figure that should be reconciled against what the call corpus actually contains.
evidence: Well, I need to do, when they ask for payment plans, I need to open wallet them. Because I've noticed I've only closed like three PIFs out of 15 deals this month.
It's bad because I'd be on like nearly 100k if I just open walleted them and if they had the money.
You haven't been getting very many deposits recently.

flags.summary: A figure of 4,500 pounds was used for the offer during the objection-handling role-play, a currency and amount outside the sanctioned $6,000/6mo and $9,000/12mo structure.
evidence: Alright. So, price drop me. / Yeah, it's 6k.

like when it comes to finances, the 4,500 pounds, like, let's say, you know, all this does for you is get you just feeling better day to day, less pain and just able to show up better. Like, would it be worth it?

flags.summary: The closer describes deliberately joining calls with his camera off so the prospect sees his shirtless profile photograph before the call starts, and the manager endorses reinstating the tactic.
evidence: I went when I was closing at 50%, I would start the call with my camera off... I would give it the join. And I'd give it like, four seconds and turn my camera on because when my camera's off, that's the profile picture.
It worked, I think, because I was closing at 50%. Give it a shot.
Because it's like, it comes up quite big, and I do look jacked in that picture.
